Free Pascal IDE / Compiler -- changelog
=======================================

Most recent version first. The IDE shows this file from
Help | What's new...


== IDE 1.0.24r / Compiler 3.3.6r ==

  Changes:
    * Asm-only inline pipeline shelved -- the Options | Compiler |
      Optimizations checkbox "Enable assembler inline" is removed,
      and the compiler hard-errors if `-OoASMINLINE' (or a
      {$OPTIMIZATION ASMINLINE} pragma, or anything in fp.cfg) tries
      to enable the bit. Known cross-unit splice and codegen bugs
      surface as occasional miscompiles (e.g. open-array length
      descriptors come back garbled, leading to runtime "Supplied
      buffer did not have enough bytes" errors from data the
      compressor produced). `-OoNOASMINLINE' is still accepted as a
      no-op so old configs and command lines keep building.
      `assembler; nostackframe; inline;' procs are emitted as a
      normal CALL.
    * `-OoASMINLINE' is hidden from `fpc -i' / `fpc -io' so it is no
      longer surfaced as a user-facing knob. The bit and option name
      are kept inside the compiler as a hook for the day the splice
      path is stable.

  No PPU format change -- units stamp 336 still applies, all 3.3.6*
  installs continue to share the same X:\fpc\units\336\ tree.


== IDE 1.0.24q / Compiler 3.3.6q ==

  New features:
    * Named arguments at call sites (off by default; opt-in). Use
      `name := value' inside an argument list to pick a parameter by
      name; positional and named arguments may mix freely so long as
      every positional argument appears before the first named one.
      Names match parameters case-insensitively (Pascal identifier
      rules) and can fill any slot, including ones the caller would
      otherwise have to skip with a sentinel placeholder:

          procedure run(target: string;
                        retries: longint = 3;
                        verbose: boolean = false);
          ...

          // positional + named, default `retries' kept:
          run('host', verbose := true);

          // all-named, declaration order ignored:
          run(verbose := true, target := 'host');

          // mixing positional and several named, in any name order:
          run('host', verbose := true, retries := 5);

      Enable per build with `-OoNAMEDARGS' on the compiler command
      line, or tick "Named arguments" under Options | Compiler |
      Optimizations in the IDE. Without the switch, `:=' inside an
      argument list parses as the existing language-level statement
      (an error in expression position), so existing code is
      unaffected.

      Errors are reported up-front: an unknown name (no parameter by
      that label), a slot filled twice, or a positional argument after
      a named one all stop the call before codegen. Mixing named
      arguments with `varargs' is rejected -- there are no formal
      names for the variadic tail. Variant-dispatch (COM Automation)
      calls keep their existing runtime-dispatch behaviour and are
      unaffected.

  No PPU format change -- units stamp 336 still applies, all 3.3.6*
  installs continue to share the same X:\fpc\units\336\ tree.


== IDE 1.0.24p / Compiler 3.3.6p ==

  Fixes:
    * Shift+Tab / Ctrl+Enter once again locates symbols after a fresh
      compile-with-browser; 1.0.24l-1.0.24o regressed most lookups to
      "symbol not found" because the compiler started recording
      reference filenames as full paths rather than basenames. Reverted
      to bare basenames; the IDE now expands them to full paths via the
      browser-info module's source-file list at lookup time, which still
      resolves include-file definitions without needing the .inc dir on
      the source-search path.


== IDE 1.0.24o / Compiler 3.3.6o ==

  New features:
    * `managed record` with per-field defaults. Prefix a record with the
      `managed` keyword (in either order with `packed`) and the compiler
      synthesises a class operator Initialize that runs on every local-var
      entry, New(), and SetLength() so each field starts at its declared
      default:

          {$mode objfpc}{$modeswitch advancedrecords}

          type
            tFrameHeader = packed managed record
              magic:   dword = $DEADBEEF;
              version: byte  = 1;
              format:  byte  = 0;
              flags:   word  = 17;
            end;

          var
            h: tFrameHeader;
          begin
            // h.magic = $DEADBEEF, h.version = 1, ... already set on entry.
          end.

      The `managed` modifier is opt-in: a plain record with `field = expr'
      is rejected ("field default requires `managed record'", err 03376),
      so existing record types keep their POD layout and zero-cost var
      entry. v1 supports single-value constants -- integer, byte/word/
      dword, boolean, char, enum, nil, real. Strings and complex
      expressions error with "field default expression too complex"
      (err 03377). A managed record that already declares `class operator
      Initialize` cannot also use field defaults (err 03378).

  Fixes:
    * `fpc -io` (i386) now lists the optimizer flags that were already parsed and honoured but missing from the advertised set: ASMINLINE, SCHEDULE, AUTOINLINE, SIZE, DEADVALUES, DEADSTORE, FORCENOSTACKFRAME, CONSTS.

  No PPU format change -- units stamp 336 still applies, all 3.3.6*
  installs continue to share the same X:\fpc\units\336\ tree.


== IDE 1.0.24n / Compiler 3.3.6n ==

  Changes:
    * `assembler; nostackframe; inline;` procs no longer auto-inline; opt
      in with `-OoASMINLINE` or via Options | Compiler | Optimizations |
      "Enable assembler inline". `-OoNOASMINLINE` stays parseable as a
      no-op for back-compat.
    * Options | Compiler | Optimizations checkboxes now read as positive
      labels ("SCC inline-first", "Enable assembler inline", "PMMX asm
      scheduler"), replacing the mixed-polarity old set; the cfg flags
      emitted on save are unchanged so existing fp.cfg files round-trip.

  No PPU format change -- units stamp 336 still applies, all 3.3.6*
  installs continue to share the same X:\fpc\units\336\ tree.


== IDE 1.0.24m / Compiler 3.3.6m ==

  * `param: T specialize [...]' now accepts enum-typed parameters.
    Previously the modifier was documented as accepting any ordinal
    type, but only `boolean' and integer values produced a compilable
    dispatch stub -- enum lists hit "Constant and CASE types do not
    match" because the synthesized case-arms emitted raw integers
    instead of enum element identifiers. The compiler now emits the
    matching element name for each value, mirroring the existing
    boolean special case:

        type
          tMode = (mOff, mOn, mDebug);

        procedure run(m: tMode specialize [mOff, mOn, mDebug];
                      n: longint);
        begin
          case m of
            mOff:   writeln('off ', n);
            mOn:    writeln('on ', n);
            mDebug: writeln('dbg ', n);
          end;
        end;

    Constant call sites still inline to a direct wrapper call; runtime
    call sites still produce the case-table dispatch.

    No PPU format change -- units stamp 336 still applies, all 3.3.6*
    installs continue to share the same X:\fpc\units\336\ tree.


== IDE 1.0.24l / Compiler 3.3.6l ==

  * Shift+Tab (Peek definition) and Ctrl+Enter (Go to definition) now
    follow symbols whose declarations live in include (.inc) files. The
    browser-info collector previously recorded only the bare basename
    for each symbol's defining position, so the editor could only open
    the file when its directory happened to be on a -Fu/-Fi search path
    -- a procedure declared in shared\poly_ref.inc and included from
    video\foo.pas would come back as "symbol not found". The full path
    is now stored alongside the line/column, so:

        (in foo.pas)
        {$I shared\poly_ref.inc}
        ...
        polyDraw_REF(...);     <- cursor here, Shift+Tab pops the peek
                                  view at shared\poly_ref.inc:2

    Same prerequisite as before: at least one successful compile with
    Options|Compiler|Browser turned on (or `-b` on the command line).

  * Alt+A (Search | Jump to asm) now works from inside an include file.
    The assembler emits one .s per compiled unit, with `# [FILE.INC]`
    markers identifying include-file spans; previously the IDE looked
    for FOO.S when the editor was on FOO.INC and gave up. The .s lookup
    now consults browser info to find the parent unit's main source and
    aims at PARENT.S, then uses the existing per-source marker matching
    to land on the right line:

        (cursor on poly_ref.inc:30, included by foo.pas)
        Alt+A  ->  opens foo.s, scrolls to the asm emitted for line 30
                   of poly_ref.inc

    If browser info hasn't been built yet you get a clear "compile with
    browser info first" message instead of the generic "no .s file".


== IDE 1.0.24k / Compiler 3.3.6k ==

  * Better i386 codegen for in-order Pentium / Pentium MMX targets
    (`-OpPENTIUM` / `-OpPENTIUMMMX`). Two peephole rules now fire
    that previously did not, producing slightly larger but
    pairing-friendlier code:

        notl  %eax            -->  xorl  $-1, %eax
        movl  $-1, %eax       -->  orl   $-1, %eax

    On the original Pentium and Pentium MMX, `not` and the 5-byte
    `mov $-1, reg` form are U-pipe-only / longer to decode; the
    `xor`/`or` rewrites pair in either pipe and the `or` form
    encodes in 3 bytes via the imm8-sign-extended opcode. Both
    rewrites stay silent under `-OpPENTIUM2` and later (where
    out-of-order execution makes the false-dep on the destination
    visible), and under `-Os` the existing size-only behaviour is
    unchanged.

    No change to PPU format -- units stamp 336 still applies, all
    3.3.6* installs continue to share the same X:\fpc\units\336\
    tree.

  * Comment-only fix in the existing `movzbl reg/mem -> xorl reg,reg ; movb`
    splitter: the rewrite is gated on `cpu_Pentium` only, not
    `cpu_PentiumMMX`. On P55C the 0Fh prefix decodes free and `movzx`
    pairs in either pipe, so the bare `movzbl` is the right output
    there. The code already had this behaviour; the comment now matches.


== IDE 1.0.24j / Compiler 3.3.6j ==

  * `{$schedule on}` / `{$schedule off}` now toggles the i386 PMMX
    scheduler uniformly across the rest of the current scope -- not
    just for the next inline asm block. Default state is whatever
    `-OoSCHEDULE` says on the command line (or the IDE's "PMMX asm
    scheduler" checkbox); the directive overrides it region-by-region:

        {$schedule on}
        procedure hot_path; begin {... scheduled ...} end;
        {$schedule off}
        procedure cold_path; begin {... not scheduled ...} end;

    The `-OoAUTOSCHEDASM` switch added in 3.3.6i is gone (it became
    redundant under the new model). The `schedule` proc modifier on
    pure-asm procs still works as a force-on override even when the
    global switch is off.

  * The PMMX scheduler now interleaves independent register chains
    that share a procedure body. A program shaped like

        movd  mm1, eax        }  chain A: mm1 RAW chain
        paddw mm1, mm1; ...   }
        movd  mm2, ebx        }  chain B: mm2 RAW chain on
        paddw mm2, mm2; ...   }            disjoint registers

    used to compile in source order (1 U/V pair, 7 cycles); the
    scheduler now reorders it to

        movd  mm1, eax | movd  mm2, ebx
        paddw mm1, mm1 | paddw mm2, mm2
        paddw mm1, mm1 | paddw mm2, mm2
        paddw mm1, mm1 | paddw mm2, mm2

    -- 4 U/V pairs, 4 cycles, ~3 cycles saved on PMMX hardware.
    Internally this drops an over-eager top-level gate ("if cur
    already pairs with prv, don't try to hoist") and iterates the
    forward walk to fixpoint so each successful hoist can unlock
    further ones upstream.

  * The scheduler now drops a `# scheduler: <module>.<proc>: N
    swap(s)` comment into the .s output of every proc it visits,
    regardless of swap count. Previously a 0-swap proc was
    indistinguishable in the .s from a proc the scheduler skipped
    entirely; now `grep "scheduler:" foo.s` answers "did the pass
    actually run on this proc" at a glance.

  * New regression test `tinlfpc_sched_cascade_chains.pp` covers the
    chain-A-then-chain-B interleaving case end-to-end (compile +
    run + verify mm1=32, mm2=56). `tinlfpc_sched_asm_mmx.pp` and
    `tinlfpc_sched_no_churn.pp` were updated -- the former now
    asserts SCHED_SWAPS_MIN=1 since the cascade fix exposes the
    interleaving opportunity its body always had; the latter's
    body was rewritten to one with genuinely no reordering room
    (4 reg-imm movs + 3 chained leas), preserving the test's role
    as a churn-guard.


== IDE 1.0.24i / Compiler 3.3.6i ==

  * Inline asm blocks AND pure-asm procs are now scheduled by default
    when the i386 PMMX scheduler is enabled. Previously every
    `asm ... end` block in a Pascal proc had to opt in via
    `{$schedule on}` ahead of it, and pure-asm procs needed the
    `schedule` proc modifier; now `-OoSCHEDULE` (or the IDE's "PMMX
    asm scheduler" checkbox) is enough -- every reorder-safe block in
    scope is fair game for the U/V pair reorderer.

    The new behaviour is gated by a new optimizer switch
    `-OoAUTOSCHEDASM` (default on). `-OoNOAUTOSCHEDASM` falls back to
    the legacy semantics: only blocks marked with `{$schedule on}` and
    pure-asm procs marked with the `schedule` modifier are touched. No
    IDE checkbox for the new switch; opt-out is command-line/fp.cfg only.

    New regression tests `tinlfpc_sched_auto_asm.pp` and
    `tinlfpc_sched_auto_pureasm.pp` cover the auto-on path for inline
    blocks and pure-asm procs respectively; the legacy negative tests
    `tinlfpc_sched_inline_asm.pp` and `tinlfpc_sched_modifier.pp` were
    updated to add `-OoNOAUTOSCHEDASM` so they keep testing the
    boundary case (block / proc left untouched without the explicit
    opt-in).


== IDE 1.0.24h / Compiler 3.3.6h ==

  * Fixed: a `specialize-set` parameter in one unit could break the
    next unit compiled in the same program build. Symptom: the FIRST
    method body parsed in the next unit suddenly failed with phantom
    "Identifier not found" or "inherited member not visible" cascades
    against members the class clearly had. Hit in the wild on
    uVesaDriver.pas (setLogicalSize lost sight of inherited
    bitsPerPixel / videoMemory) whenever a unit earlier in the build
    used a specialize-set parameter. The fix is internal -- no source
    changes needed.



  * i386 PMMX scheduler -- much smarter. The U/V reorderer added in
    3.3.6c learned three new tricks:

      - MMX-aware. MMX arithmetic, compares, logicals, pack/unpack
        and movd/movq now count as pairable; MMX multiplies and
        shifts pair too, but only on the U pipe (so two PMULLWs in
        a row no longer get falsely paired). EMMS, FEMMS, PUSH /
        POP, ENTER / LEAVE became hard barriers and are never
        reordered across.

      - Wider window. The old pass only looked at the immediate
        [pairable, non-pairable, pairable] shape. The new pass
        walks back up to 8 instructions from each pairable slot
        looking for a partner, skipping intermediates as long as
        every adjacent swap stays safe.

      - No-op-pair detection. Skips swaps that would just shuffle
        which adjacency carries an already-paired instruction --
        zero benefit, real .s diff, not worth doing.

    Per-swap markers and -vd output from 3.3.6f carry through
    unchanged: every applied swap drops a `# sched-swap' line into
    the .s, and -vd shows per-swap / per-proc / per-unit /
    per-compile counts.

    test-lite gained `%SCHED_SWAPS_MIN=N' and `%SCHED_SWAPS_MAX=N'
    directives for range assertions; `%SCHED_SWAPS=N' keeps its
    exact-match semantics.


== IDE 1.0.24f / Compiler 3.3.6f ==

  * i386 PMMX scheduler now reports what it did. Each successful
    [P, NP, P] -> [P, P, NP] hoist drops a `# sched-swap' comment
    into the .s at the swap site, so a developer (or test harness)
    can see exactly which instructions were paired. -vd adds a
    one-line per-swap detail, plus per-proc and per-unit summary
    lines:

        [scheduler] swap: mov | shl | mov -> mov | mov | shl
        [scheduler] system.fpc_ansistr_assign: 4 swap(s) (~4 cy)
        [scheduler] unit system: 73 swap(s) (~73 cy)

    A per-compile grand total surfaces at default verbosity (no -v
    flag needed) when the scheduler fired at least once:

        [scheduler] total: 1832 swap(s) (~1832 cy)

    Cycle estimate is N x 1 -- each swap forms exactly one new U/V
    pair on PMMX, saving one straight-line cycle. No loop weighting.
    Two new regression tests bracket the behaviour:
    `tinlfpc_sched_visible_swap' (positive control: hand-crafted
    [movl, shll, movl, addl] in a `schedule;' asm proc; expects
    exactly one marker) and `tinlfpc_sched_asm_mmx' (MMX inline-asm
    body opted in via `{$schedule on}'; expects zero markers under
    v1's integer-only pairable set). The lite-suite directive
    %SCHED_SWAPS=N (with optional %SCHED_SWAPS_MIN/_MAX bounds)
    asserts the marker count after a successful compile.

  * `RDTSC' compiler intrinsic on i386. New inline node `in_x86_rdtsc'
    binds the i386 RDTSC opcode (read time-stamp counter) into a
    64-bit qword result via the standard EDX:EAX register-pair
    pattern, so a Pascal-only `cStart'/`cStop' can read the TSC
    without an asm block. When nothing else is live in EAX/EDX the
    regalloc collapses the body to the bare RDTSC at the call site.
    i386 only for now -- x86_64 also returns EDX:EAX but combining
    them into a single 64-bit register needs a shl/or pair we haven't
    implemented yet. Exposed via `intrinsics' unit; smoke test in
    tinlfpc_rdtsc.

  * ppudump now builds clean again. Commit 2397daec6b6 (IDE
    checkboxes for asm-only inline + PMMX scheduler) added three
    new enum values -- `cs_schedule_asm', `cs_opt_asm_inline',
    `po_schedule_asm' -- without updating the parallel string and
    mask arrays in ppudump.pp, so `make utils_all' bombed with
    "Expected another 1 array elements". Three one-line additions.


== IDE 1.0.24e / Compiler 3.3.6e ==

  * IDE Options | Compiler | Optimizations grew two new checkboxes for
    the recent asm-related compiler switches:

      [ ] No asm-only inline       (cs_opt_asm_inline -- default ON)
      [ ] PMMX asm scheduler       (cs_opt_scheduler  -- default OFF)

    The first is the kill-switch for the still-experimental asm-only
    inline pipeline (cross-unit splice, register-cc paras, register
    return). When ticked, fp.cfg gets -OoNOASMINLINE and
    is_assembler_inlineable rejects every candidate up-front; an
    `assembler; nostackframe; inline;' proc is then emitted as a
    normal CALL. Useful when chasing a compile-time crash that's
    suspected to be in the splice path -- flip the box, recompile,
    see whether the crash goes away.

    The second exposes the PMMX U/V pair scheduler (added in 3.3.6c)
    as an IDE-discoverable toggle. Tick it to add -OoSCHEDULE; pair
    with the Processor tab's PENTIUM or PENTIUMMMX target for it to
    actually fire (the scheduler early-exits on other CPUs).

    Both switches are also reachable via the command line (-OoXXXX),
    fp.cfg, and the new test-play.ps1 harness's -NoAsmInline /
    -Scheduler flags.

  * test-play.ps1 -- new go32v2-native regression-test harness for
    dev\video\play.pas. Mirrors test-lite.ps1 in spirit (run-after-
    rebuild, exit-code-gated) but cross-compiles inside DOSBox-X with
    cycles=max + core=dynamic, captures compile.txt for crash
    analysis, and supports the two flags above for bisecting compiler
    regressions against play.pas without touching dev\video\.


== IDE 1.0.24d / Compiler 3.3.6d ==

  * `specialize-set' parameters can now declare a default value:

        procedure dith(k: integer specialize [1, 4, 8] = 4);
        procedure flag(b: boolean specialize [true, false] = true);

    Callers can omit the argument; `dith()' is the same as
    `dith(4)', and the constant-call collapse to a direct call
    into the matching specialisation works for the omitted-arg
    form too.

    The default is required to be a member of the set -- writing
    `k: integer specialize [1, 4, 8] = 2' is rejected at compile
    time, because the compiler-generated case-table dispatch has
    no else arm and a stray default would otherwise fall through
    at runtime.

== IDE 1.0.24c / Compiler 3.3.6c ==

  * Pascal-style block comments (`{...}', `(*...*)', `//...') inside
    a `specialize-set' asm body no longer break the next unrelated
    proc. Pre-fix, an asm body that contained a `{...}' or `//'
    comment confused the per-value wrapper synthesis enough that the
    next proc in the same unit failed to parse with cascading
    "Unrecognized opcode ASM" errors. All three comment forms now
    work inside specset-asm bodies.

  * `schedule' proc modifier and `{$schedule on}' directive let
    user-written asm opt in to the i386 PMMX U/V scheduler:

        procedure foo; assembler; nostackframe; schedule;
        ...

        {$schedule on}
        asm
          ...
        end;

    The default behaviour stays "skip user asm" so existing code is
    untouched; the modifier flips po_schedule_asm on the procdef so
    psub.pas runs the scheduler over the body anyway, and the
    directive stamps cs_schedule_asm onto the asm-block marker so
    TAsmScheduler.Optimize processes the block. Both flags are
    masked off at PPU boundaries, so they stay local-compile-time
    hints and don't move the .ppu format.

  * i386 PMMX U/V pair-aware reorderer (post-peephole, opt-in).
    A new compiler/i386/schedi386.pas walks each basic block looking
    for [UV-pairable, non-pairable, UV-pairable] shapes and hoists
    the third instruction past the second so the first and third
    issue together as a U/V pair on Pentium / Pentium-MMX. Net
    saving on PMMX is one cycle per applied swap. Gated by
    `-OoSCHEDULE' plus `-Op[PENTIUM | PENTIUMMMX]'; default OFF;
    -O2/-O3 do not pull it in. Use `{$schedule on}' (above) to
    extend the pass to user asm blocks.

  * `assembler; nostackframe; inline;' procs now accept default-
    valued parameters. The gate that rejected them was a stale
    belt-and-braces from before the asm-inline PPU round-trip fix;
    omitted optional args are now materialised as
    `genconstsymtree(defaultconstsym)' and flow through the v2(c)
    hoist+rcd_load splice path with no codegen changes. Verified
    on same-unit and cross-unit (PPU round-trip) shapes.


== IDE 1.0.24b / Compiler 3.3.6b ==

  * Const-prop / DFA now runs on Pascal procs that inline pure-asm
    helpers. Pre-fix, a single inline-asm helper call (e.g.
    `cStart(slot)') inside a 200-line Pascal procedure disabled
    constant propagation, dead-store elimination, and branch folding
    for the whole rest of the procedure -- well past the splice
    site. The optimiser now recognises the spliced asm body as
    "validated pure-asm helper" and keeps DFA enabled. User-written
    `asm ... end;` blocks in your own code still disable DFA on the
    enclosing proc as before; only spliced clones of inline-asm
    helpers get the new treatment.


== IDE 1.0.24a / Compiler 3.3.6a ==

  * Inline-asm constant-arg specialisation. When the caller passes
    an integer literal or `nil` to a register-cc parameter of a
    pure-asm `inline` proc, the compiler now loads the constant
    straight into the para's home register instead of routing it
    through a stack temp. Net effect at every such call site: one
    `mov reg, $imm` instead of `mov [slot], $imm ; mov reg, [slot]`.
    Common case for `myinline(0, x)`, flag/mask args, etc.

  * Clearer error when a `.ppu` file is from a different compiler
    version. The previous wording was just "Can't compile unit FOO,
    no sources available", with the actual cause ("PPU Invalid
    Version") buried at the unusual `-vu' verbosity level. The
    fatal line now spells out the version mismatch directly --
    the usual fix is to delete the old `.ppu' or rebuild against
    the matching compiler.


== IDE 1.0.24 / Compiler 3.3.6 ==

  * Cross-unit asm-inline now actually inlines instead of crashing
    the compiler or producing corrupt object files. A helper like
    cStart declared `assembler; nostackframe; inline;` in one unit
    and called from another now splices into the caller -- no more
    `Page Fault at eip=0` / EAccessViolation when compiling
    dev/video, no more `Undefined symbol: <garbled>` from the
    linker. Same-unit asm-inline is unchanged.

  * Version renumbered to follow the rule: bump the third digit
    only when the .ppu format changes; otherwise add a letter
    suffix. The previous "3.3.9c" lineage was a c-bump series
    where the .ppu format never actually changed -- they have all
    been retroactively rewritten as 3.3.5* letter suffixes in this
    changelog (see entries below). This release is the first true
    PPU-breaking bump since 3.3.5, so it lands as 3.3.6, and the
    shared units now sit at `X:\fpc\units\336\`. The old
    `X:\fpc\units\335\` (and any earlier) trees stay intact for any
    pre-3.3.6 install you still need to use.


== IDE 1.0.23c / Compiler 3.3.5g ==

  * `%if` inside `asm` blocks of `specialize-set` procedures.
    Conditional asm gated on a specialize-set parameter now folds
    correctly per specialisation:

        procedure yog_to_16_mmx(page: tYOG420; yofs: integer = 0;
                                use_dither: boolean specialize [true, false]);
        begin
          asm
            ...
            %if use_dither
              paddusb mm4, dither8[eax*8]
              paddusb mm5, dither4[eax*8]
              paddusb mm6, dither8[eax*8]
            %endif
            ...
          end;
        end;

    Two specialised copies are emitted -- one with the conditional
    block spliced in, one without -- and the dispatch stub folds
    constant call sites to a direct call into the matching wrapper.

  * Asm const-expression evaluator handles untyped ordinal constants.
    `%if` (and `db`, `dw`, etc.) accepts an in-scope `const k = N;`
    or `const k = TRUE;` reference and inlines the integer value.
    Boolean/char/enum/integer constants all work; the previous
    behaviour was "wrong sym type" for any non-staticvar const.

  * Wrapper procs synthesised by specialize-set inherit the source
    proc's `inline;' directive instead of being unconditionally
    marked inline. Asm-bodied wrappers (and any other body that
    triggers `pio_inline_not_possible') now stay regular calls,
    avoiding spurious notes -- the dispatch stub is still inline,
    so constant call sites continue to fold to a direct call.


== IDE 1.0.23b / Compiler 3.3.5f ==

  * `codegen-proc` parameter modifier (v5). A parameter declared
    `codegen` lets the body of the proc emit a single inline-asm
    template that the compiler patches per call site with the
    actual operand of that argument. Both immediate and pointer
    operands are supported, including memory-displacement patch
    sites (e.g. `mov eax, [ebx + arg]`). One template, many
    specialised emit sites -- no per-call thunk, no register
    shuffling.

  * `assembler; nostackframe; inline;` accepts cross-register
    reads of register-cc parameters. Previously the body had to
    consume each register-cc param from the register the calling
    convention placed it in (eax/edx/ecx for the first three
    integer args). Now the body may read `arg` from a different
    register and the compiler rewrites the access at splice time.
    Lets you write the body in whatever register layout suits the
    instruction sequence rather than the cc.

  * Quieter inline diagnostics. `-vy` no longer echoes a "Not
    inlining ..." line for every call site of a proc the parser
    already rejected once (self-recursion, pio_inline_not_possible,
    missing inlining-info). Per-call-site diagnostics are now
    reserved for site-specific reasons -- SCC defer, budget
    exceeded, hidden-symbol cross-unit, unsafe param construct.


== IDE 1.0.23a / Compiler 3.3.5e ==

  * New `specialize-set` parameter modifier. When a parameter
    only ever takes a few known constant values, you can list
    them and the compiler will generate a fast specialised
    path for each:

        procedure f(a: integer; k: integer specialize [1, 4, 8]);
        begin
          writeln(a + k * 100);
        end;

    Constant call sites collapse to a direct call into the
    matching specialisation; variable call sites become a small
    case-table dispatch. Set syntax accepts literals, named
    consts, and ranges: [1, 4, 8], [0..3], [0, 2, 4..7]. Up to
    64 specialisations per proc; parameter type must be ordinal.

    Limitations in this first cut: no methods (class/record/
    object); only one specialize-set parameter per proc; can't
    self-recurse from inside the body; can't mix with regular
    overloads of the same name in the same scope.


== IDE 1.0.23 / Compiler 3.3.5d ==

  * Intel asm conditionals. `%if / %elseif / %else / %endif`
    now work inside Intel-syntax asm blocks, with the usual
    integer arithmetic and in-scope const references in the
    condition. AT&T asm is unchanged.

  * Inlining is more aggressive by default. The classic depth-
    decay formula has been replaced with a flat per-call-site
    budget (1000 nodes), so mid-sized helpers no longer get
    rejected just for being four calls deep. To restore the
    previous behaviour: `-OoINLINESITEBUDGET=0`.

  * Better diagnostics when an `assembler; inline;` proc is
    rejected. Instead of the bare "assembler not yet supported
    inside inline procedure", the compiler now tells you exactly
    why -- missing `nostackframe`, unsupported parameter type,
    wrong calling convention, etc.

  * Inline-tuning knobs. Four `-Oo<KEY>=N` options to tune
    inlining policy:
        -OoINLINEAUTOLIMIT=N    auto-inline gate (default 25)
        -OoINLINEHARDCAP=N      hard per-site body cap
        -OoINLINEGROWTHCAP=N    cumulative growth cap per proc
        -OoINLINESITEBUDGET=N   flat per-site budget (default 1000;
                                set 0 for the legacy depth formula)
    Use `-vy` to see why a call wasn't inlined and `-vd` to see
    auto-inline decisions.


== IDE 1.0.18 .. 1.0.22 / Compiler 3.3.4, 3.3.5, 3.3.5a, 3.3.5b, 3.3.5c ==

(These features rolled in over several versions. Listed here
together because they form one coherent extension to inline
assembler. Versions 3.3.6..3.3.9 in earlier drafts of this file
have been renumbered as 3.3.5a..3.3.5c -- those bumps did not
change the .ppu format and so do not warrant a c-digit bump under
the current rule. 3.3.4 + 3.3.5 are the legitimate c-bumps in this
range.)

  * Inline assembler functions. Procedures and functions
    declared `assembler; nostackframe; inline;` are now spliced
    directly into the caller -- no `call`/`ret`, just the body's
    instructions emitted in place. This started as zero-arg
    void-return procs and grew incrementally:

      - bodies may reference globals and typed constants
      - bodies may use local labels and branch between them;
        each splice gets its own fresh set of labels so the same
        helper can be inlined many times in one routine
      - functions may return a value when the result fits in a
        single integer register (longint, dword, pointer, ...)
      - parameters may be taken in registers (the default
        `register;` cc on i386 puts the first three integer args
        in `%eax`, `%edx`, `%ecx`, and the body sees them there
        directly -- no need to name them in the body)

    Combined, these let you write things like:

        function add(a, b: longint): longint;
          register; assembler; nostackframe; inline;
        asm
          addl %edx, %eax
        end;

    and have `x := add(1, 2) + add(3, 4);` collapse to four
    inline `addl` instructions plus the loads needed by the
    caller. Stack-passed args, by-reference params (var/out/
    constref), FPU/MM-register params, and float/multi-register
    returns are still rejected by the gate.

    Treat this as a useful but lightly-tested extension. If a
    pure-asm proc that compiled fine before suddenly errors or
    produces strange code, the inliner is the first thing to
    suspect -- removing the `inline;` directive is a quick way
    to confirm.

  * `var x: T align N;` for static globals. Lets a single
    declaration request stricter alignment than the target's
    default cap -- handy for MMX/SSE scratch globals on go32v2
    that need 8/16-byte alignment without a getmem-and-align
    dance:

        var mmreg : qword align 8;
        var sse_buf : array[0..3] of single align 16;

    N must be a power of two in 1..128. Initialised vars
    (`var x: T align N = init;`) are limited to N <= 4 on
    go32v2 (DJGPP COFF object-format constraint); the compiler
    raises an error rather than silently clamping. Locals and
    parameters are not aligned (the prologue does not realign
    ESP).


== IDE 1.0.17 / Compiler 3.3.3 ==

  * Quick-Open (Ctrl+U): typing a `.` in the filter now matches
    the full basename, so files outside the editor's mask (e.g.
    `play.log`) show up as you type. Pressing Enter on an entry
    with a `.` that has no listbox match resolves the literal
    text against the project dir and every -Fu/-Fi search dir
    and opens it if found.

  * File|Open, File|Open Recent, and OpenSearch no longer open
    a second editor window when the file is already open --
    they focus the existing window instead. (File|New still
    creates a fresh untitled window.) Stops the same file
    ending up loaded twice with diverging unsaved edits.


== IDE 1.0.16 / Compiler 3.3.3 ==

IDE
  * Quick-Open (Ctrl+U): mask textbox to filter the file list
    by extension or name pattern; persists across sessions.
    Result list sorts so .pas/.pp sources show ahead of .ppu/.o
    build artefacts.
  * DOS Shell: command prompt is marked so you can tell you're
    in a shell-out; refuses to re-enter while one is already
    running -- avoids the stacked-IDE / leaked-temp-files trap.
  * Editor color fixes; new INI and ASM file syntax highlighting.
  * Run profiles: named bundles of (main file, run params),
    switchable from the Run menu. Per-project, persisted with
    the desktop.
  * Alt+Up / Alt+Down: jump between interface declaration and
    implementation of the procedure under the cursor.
  * Ctrl+Enter go-to-definition; Alt+Left / Alt+Right back/
    forward navigation history (browser-style).
  * Shift+Tab peek-definition popup -- shows the declaration of
    the symbol under the cursor without leaving your spot.
  * Find in Files: dialog state (last query, mask, options)
    persists across sessions; fixed a command-code clash that
    was triggering Comment-selection instead.
  * Search | Jump to Asm: grayed out when no source is focused.
  * Wordstar prefix chord (Ctrl-K, Ctrl-Q) no longer eats its
    second key when that key matches a menu hot-key letter
    (e.g. Ctrl-K W).
  * Help | What's new...: this dialog.
  * About box and splash banner now show "-O3" suffix when the
    binary was built with the -O3 chain.

Compiler
  * Faster symbol browsing on large projects (browcol switched
    from a sorted collection to a hash table -- the old
    O(N log N) insert dominated on big projects).


== IDE 1.0.15 / Compiler 3.3.2 ==

First version to stamp the build commit short hash into the
binary banners (e.g. "3.3.2-a885a49" / "1.0.15-a885a49").

IDE
  * Ctrl+U Quick-Open by filename across project + -Fu/-Fi paths.
  * Find in Files (Ctrl+Shift+F), results in the Messages window.
  * Search | Jump to Asm Source (Alt+A); auto-recompiles -al if
    needed.
  * Open source files maximized + optional chromeless full-screen
    mode (F5 toggles); two new flags in Options | Editor.
  * S3-specific wide text-mode probe runs after VBE enumeration
    so S3-family chipsets expose the 100/132-column modes that
    the BIOS hides.
  * Recent Files uses move-to-front MRU on every open.
  * DOS Shell / File|Open anchor to the IDE's launch directory.
  * Pentium CPU-target menu labels corrected (-CpPENTIUM2 was
    mis-labelled "PentiumMMX" -- selecting it on a real P55C
    crashed with invalid-opcode / page fault).

Compiler (i386)
  * New PENTIUMMMX cputype (P55C; P5 + MMX, no CMOV) between
    Pentium and Pentium 2.
  * -CpPENTIUM4 and friends now auto-define CPUX86_HAS_MMX /
    _SSEUNIT / _SSE2 to match the selected cputype -- no manual
    -d flags needed.
  * Faster integer multiply by 2^n +/- 1 (peephole now lowers
    these to lea/shl + add/sub).

RTL (i386 / go32v2)
  * MMX FillChar / FillWord / FillDWord / FillQWord variants,
    auto-dispatched on MMX-capable CPUs without SSE2.
  * Move: startup probe detects broken 64-bit-precision emulator
    FPUs (em-dosbox, 86Box default) and falls back to a plain
    rep-movsl path that avoids x87 entirely.
  * Text-mode cursor scales to the actual VGA font height
    (16 scan lines in 80x25) instead of a hardcoded 7.
